title: What Happens If You Hold In Your Pee?
description:
What Happens If You Hold In Your Pee?

StatPearls, 'Urinary Retention', NCBI Bookshelf NBK538522 (updated 2024)

Full sources:
- StatPearls, 'Urinary Retention', NCBI Bookshelf NBK538522 (updated 2024): normal bladder capacity 400-600 mL; chronic retention is defined by volumes over 300 mL; long-term retention carries risk of urinary tract infection, bladder damage (detrusor changes, stones, diverticula) and chronic kidney failure; untreated obstruction can cause hydronephrosis (kidney congestion)
- StatPearls, 'Bladder Rupture', NCBI Bookshelf NBK513246 (updated 2024): bladder rupture is rare; the great majority of cases follow blunt trauma (or instrumentation) on a full bladder - ordinary voluntary holding by a healthy person is not a documented cause
- NIH/MedlinePlus-cited review of urinary retention (Siamoulosis/Siamoulidou 2014 classification; Wikipedia, accessed 2026-11-14): acute retention is a medical emergency; micturition urge arises from bladder-wall stretch receptors signaling the brain (micturition reflex)

Not medical advice — sources linked for every claim.
